title: Two plans of Tŷ Mawr

cast.E_AGENT: the land surveyor drawing the plan of Tŷ Mawr
cast.C_FRED: a drover crossing the yard with cattle

shots.direction: About 7 seconds. Date-and-place card over an establishing still. Early morning, late 18th century. Tŷ Mawr's long stone farmhouse and outbuildings stand round a muddy yard on Llandough hill, which is inland. Beyond the hedges the ground falls away to the Ely valley and grey marshland under low cloud. A slow push-in from the gateway. Ambience: rooks, a distant cow, wind in the hedges.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 establishing still, Glamorgan, Wales, c. 1790, early morning. A long whitewashed rubble-stone farmhouse with a slate and thatch roofline and low stone outbuildings around a muddy farmyard with puddles and straw. A wooden field gate in the foreground and hawthorn hedges. The land slopes down inland to a river valley and flat grey marshes under low cloud, with no sea and no coastline. Soft overcast light, muted greens and browns, period-accurate, no people, no text, no heraldry.

shots.direction: About 8 seconds. Wide still with a slow lateral drift. The surveyor stands in the yard beside a plane table on a wooden tripod. Paper is pinned to the board, and a brass sighting rule and a coiled measuring chain lie beside it. Through the gate behind him a drover drives a few black cattle into the yard with a hazel stick. Ambience: hooves in mud, the chain clinking, a dog barking once.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 still, Welsh farmyard, c. 1790. A pale clean-shaven man in his 50s wears thin-rimmed spectacles, a dark wool frock coat, a waistcoat, breeches, boots and a dark round hat. He stands at a wooden plane table on a tripod with paper pinned to it, a brass alidade on top, and a leather document case and a coiled iron surveyor's chain at his feet. In the background a lean man in his 30s with sandy hair and a moustache, wearing a long coarse wool coat, a battered felt hat and gaiters, drives four black Welsh cattle through a wooden gate with a hazel stick. The ground is muddy, the light overcast, the style period-accurate. Invented faces, no text, no heraldry.

shots.direction: About 9 seconds. Medium shot of the drover, who pulls up beside the plane table as the cattle mill behind him. He is half amused and half wary, and he speaks to the surveyor.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 medium shot, Welsh farmyard, c. 1790. A lean man in his 30s with sandy hair, a moustache and a shy half-smile wears a long coarse brown wool coat and a battered felt hat, and leans on a hazel drover's stick. Black cattle stand behind him in the mud. Soft overcast light, period-accurate. Invented face, no text, no heraldry.

lines.accent: South Wales (Glamorgan) Welsh, rural; NATIVE REVIEW NEEDED
lines.cy: Bore da, syr. Gofalwch am y bwrdd 'na, ma'r da 'ma'n moyn yr hewl i gyd. Beth y'ch chi'n neud 'ma, 'te?
lines.en: Morning, sir. Mind that board, these cattle want the whole road. What are you doing here, then?
lines.es: Buen día, señor. Cuidado con ese tablero, que estas vacas quieren todo el camino. ¿Y qué anda haciendo acá?

shots.direction: About 8 seconds. Medium close-up of the surveyor. He does not look up at first. He sights along the brass rule toward the farmhouse corner, makes a pencil mark, and only then answers.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 medium close-up, c. 1790. A pale clean-shaven man in his 50s with thin-rimmed spectacles, a dark wool frock coat and a dark round hat bends over a plane table and sights along a brass alidade, holding a pencil over pinned paper with faint pencil lines. A whitewashed farmhouse wall is blurred behind him. Overcast light, period-accurate. Invented face, no legible text, no heraldry.

lines.accent: South Wales Welsh, educated and measured; NATIVE REVIEW NEEDED
lines.cy: Tynnu cynllun o fferm y Tŷ Mawr. Y fferm i gyd, fel y mae hi heddi, i'r gadwyn.
lines.en: Drawing a plan of Tŷ Mawr farm. The whole farm, as it lies today, to the chain.
lines.es: Dibujo un plano de la chacra de Tŷ Mawr. Toda entera, tal como está hoy, medida con la cadena.

shots.direction: About 5 seconds. Back on the drover, who pushes his hat back, curious.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 medium shot, c. 1790. A lean sandy-haired man in his 30s with a moustache, a long wool coat and a felt hat pushed back on his head looks across with curiosity. A black cow's head is in the foreground out of focus, and a muddy farmyard lies behind him. Overcast, period-accurate. Invented face, no text, no heraldry.

lines.accent: South Wales (Glamorgan) Welsh, rural; NATIVE REVIEW NEEDED
lines.cy: I bwy, 'te? Pwy sy'n talu am waith fel 'na?
lines.en: For whom, then? Who pays for work like that?
lines.es: ¿Para quién, entonces? ¿Quién paga un trabajo así?

shots.direction: About 12 seconds. The surveyor straightens and taps the head of the sheet with his pencil, where the title will be inked. He is dry and businesslike. The writing on the paper is not legible to camera.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 medium close-up, c. 1790. A pale clean-shaven surveyor in his 50s with thin-rimmed spectacles and a dark frock coat straightens at his plane table and taps the top margin of a pinned paper sheet with a pencil. His expression is dry and businesslike. A farmyard and stone outbuildings are soft behind him, under overcast light. Period-accurate. Invented face, no legible text, no heraldry.

lines.accent: South Wales Welsh, educated and measured; the phrase 'Gedrych property' is spoken in English as it is written on the plan; NATIVE REVIEW NEEDED
lines.cy: Eiddo Gedrych yw e. 'Gedrych property', dyna fydd ar ben y papur. Pwy sy'n ei ffermo, nid 'y musnes i yw hynny. Caeau dw i'n eu cyfri, nid pobol.
lines.en: It's Gedrych property. 'Gedrych property', that's what goes at the head of the sheet. Who farms it is no business of mine. I count fields, not people.
lines.es: Es propiedad Gedrych. 'Gedrych property', eso va arriba del papel. Quién la trabaja no es asunto mío. Yo cuento campos, no gente.

shots.direction: About 7 seconds. The drover glances over his shoulder at the sky over the valley, then back at the surveyor with a grin, and moves his stick to set the cattle going.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 medium shot, c. 1790. A lean sandy-haired drover in his 30s with a moustache, a long wool coat and a felt hat grins over his shoulder and raises a hazel stick. Dark rain clouds gather over an inland river valley and flat marshes behind him, and black cattle stand in a muddy farmyard. Period-accurate. Invented face, no text, no heraldry.

lines.accent: South Wales (Glamorgan) Welsh, rural; NATIVE REVIEW NEEDED
lines.cy: Wel, cyfrwch yn glou, syr. Ma'r glaw'n dod lan o'r morfa.
lines.en: Well, count quickly, sir. The rain's coming up off the marsh.
lines.es: Bueno, cuente rápido, señor. La lluvia ya viene subiendo la loma desde los bañados.

shots.direction: About 10 seconds. Slow overhead push onto the plane table. The surveyor's hand inks a fine boundary line around field shapes in pencil, with the house drawn as a small block. No writing is legible. Ambience: the pen scratching and the first drops of rain on paper.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 overhead close-up, c. 1790. A hand in a dark wool cuff holds a quill and inks fine boundary lines over pencil field outlines on cream laid paper pinned to a wooden plane table. A small rectangle marks a farmhouse, and a brass alidade, an inkwell and a few raindrops sit on the paper. Period-accurate surveying, no legible text, no heraldry, no crest or cartouche emblem.

captions.text: c. 1790: plan of Ty Mawr farm, Llandough, then 'Gedrych property' (Glamorgan Archives DMAT/279) (CH-0005)

shots.direction: About 9 seconds. Wide still with a slow pull-back. The drover drives the cattle out through the far gate as the rain thickens. The surveyor, alone in the yard, shelters his board under his coat-tail. Ambience: rain, hooves fading.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 wide still, Welsh farmyard, c. 1790, in light rain. A drover in a long wool coat drives black cattle out through a far wooden gate. In the foreground a surveyor in a dark frock coat and round hat shields a plane table with the skirt of his coat. A whitewashed stone farmhouse and outbuildings stand around him, with wet mud, grey light and inland hills. Period-accurate. Invented faces, no text, no heraldry.

captions.text: c. 1800: a second plan of Ty Mawr farm, Llandough, is drawn (Glamorgan Archives DXJF/61/12) (CH-0006)

shots.direction: About 10 seconds. Closing landscape still from the same moment. A slow tilt from the farm's top field up the open hillside of Llandough, with the Ely and the marshes below and Leckwith woods across the valley under rain. No school is shown; the caption carries the later event. Ambience: rain, wind, rooks.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 landscape still, c. 1790, inland Glamorgan in rain. An open green hillside with hedged fields and a few scattered stone cottages slopes down to a winding river and flat grey marshes, with dark woods on the far side of the valley. Low rain clouds, no sea and no coastline, no modern buildings, period-accurate. No people, no text, no heraldry.

continuity: The surveyor rolls the wet sheet into his leather case. Cut to the Bute estate office, where an agent checks plan 19 of Stewart's survey, 'Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm'.
